headline: High: shared state and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application files and shares state via a checkpointer store, while next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language commands. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in shared files or diagrams can influence downstream instructions. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same checkpointer-backed workspace or file set
IF next-ai-draw-io ingests diagram/text content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
Review MCP tool outputs before execution
requires-engineering: enforce content-safety filters on shared state

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and handle files or graph state that may contain sensitive application data or API keys. LangGraph explicitly touches graph state and secrets; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams. Shared storage or copied artifacts could leak data through either agent's outbound API calls.
conditions: IF sensitive graph state or documents are placed in a shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to external model providers by default
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared folders
Use separate API keys per agent
Turn off upload of full file contents where possible
Redact secrets before processing
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write filesystem state and spawn subprocesses; next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and broad network egress. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared files or external resources if pointed at the same workspace, so write conflicts are plausible in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF MCP tools expose mutable shared resources without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Restrict MCP tools to read-only where possible
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a stateful orchestration layer, and next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands for AI-assisted visualization. If LangGraph-generated content is fed into next-ai-draw-io without verification, errors can propagate into diagrams or actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly observed.
conditions: IF LangGraph output is treated as authoritative input by next-ai-draw-io
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require citations or schema checks on LangGraph output
Show diffs before rendering diagrams
Limit next-ai-draw-io to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph is open-source library infrastructure with graph-state handling, while next-ai-draw-io processes documents and sends requests to multiple external AI providers. If regulated documents or EU PII flow through the pair, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The other agent is not cited separately because the compliance concern is driven mainly by next-ai-draw-io's outbound provider set.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or customer documents are processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or residency controls for the chosen model provider
mitigations: Route regulated data only to approved providers
Minimize retention in both tools
Document data flows and residency
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
requires-engineering: implement policy-based provider routing
